notes: §1985:VII.3.2.4 GR2 says the BLOCK CONTAINS, CODE-SET, DATA RECORDS, LABEL RECORDS, LINAGE, RECORD and VALUE OF clauses "are presented in alphabetical order on the following pages": a statement of where the standard prints the seven clauses, with no requirement on a program or on the object program (the order of the clauses in source is §1985:VII.3.2.3 SR2's: "The clauses which follow file-name-1 may appear in any order."). What the compiler owes the rule is that each clause it names is a clause of the sequential file description entry at 85: each is an alternative of fileDescriptionClause, FileDescriptionFormats.Rows admits each in the sequential format, and the three clauses 2002 deletes (LABEL RECORDS, DATA RECORDS, VALUE OF) are accepted at --std 85 by their edition arms VisitLabelRecordsClause, VisitDataRecordsClause and VisitValueOfClause, which refuse them from 2002. Probed at 85: one sequential FD writing all seven, in the rule's alphabetical order and in another order (VALUE OF first, BLOCK CONTAINS last), compiles and runs. The rules of each clause are their own rows (the operand rules of DATA RECORDS, LABEL RECORDS and VALUE OF are kb/Work PB5070). The witness writes BLOCK CONTAINS, DATA RECORD, LABEL RECORDS and RECORD CONTAINS on one FD and writes a record.

next.reason: 1985 GR2 only says the BLOCK CONTAINS, CODE-SET, DATA RECORDS, LABEL RECORDS, LINAGE, RECORD and VALUE OF clauses 'are presented in alphabetical order on the following pages': a note on the document's layout, with no requirement on a program or implementation. 2023 states no presentation order (the word 'alphabetical' does not occur in specs/ISO_COBOL_2023.md); its file description clauses are subclauses of §2023:13.18, and the order of clauses in source is a different matter. No rule carries it; no program's meaning depends on it.
